correctness.rationale: For an interior point in the positive quadrant the largest corner projection strictly exceeds the squared norm; membership in just one closed disk requires the squared norm to strictly exceed the second projection |tx-y|. Axes tie. In polar coordinates the radial fiber has lower endpoint |t cos(theta)-sin(theta)| and upper endpoint min(t/cos(theta),1/sin(theta)). The only loss of a nonempty fiber occurs for 1/t<tan(theta)<t at 2 tan(theta)^2 - t tan(theta) + 1 <= 0. The double root removes the entire ray already at equality. The positive fibers are open intervals with continuous endpoints and hence connected over each surviving angular interval. Independently, Cartesian slicing yields F(t)=3/2-(1/(2t))*integral from 0 to min(3,sqrt(1+t^2)) of sqrt(1+t^2-z^2) dz. Indeed the two excluded horizontal widths are (sqrt(t^2+4y(1-y))-t)/2 and sqrt(max(0,t^2-4y(y+1))); they are disjoint. The omitted circular cap has height h=sqrt(1+t^2)-3. Rescaling its integral yields h^(3/2) times a smooth positive factor, proving C^1, failure of twice differentiability, and the stated coefficient 2*2^(1/4)/9. Differentiation of G_t confirms the equivalent angular antiderivative.
residual_risks: Cartesian high-precision tests at eight aspect ratios and four cusp offsets are finite corroboration only. The analytic proof covers the continuum and critical equality.

evidence: For the positive quadrant, the twofold region is exactly x^2+y^2<=|tx-y|; its bottom lobe meets the top edge iff x(t-x)>=2, while the left lobe cannot meet the right edge when t>=1.

On every open-quadrant ray both disk-incidence and rectangular membership are radial cutoffs; the singleton fiber is the interval strictly between the twofold cutoff and the rectangular edge. A vanishing fiber corresponds exactly to a twofold contact at that edge.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The stated inequalities make the forbidden angular set empty below the threshold, a single ray at equality (the closed bottom lobe reaches the excluded edge at x=t/2), and a closed interval above. Continuous nonempty fibers give one or two components per quadrant and the tied axes separate quadrants. This count is a direct consequence of the compared geometry, not an independent unresolved classification.
